record.paper_title: Open questions for strongly interacting Fermi gases with zero-range interactions
record.context_brief: Phonon damping near zero acoustic curvature
record.original_question: For low-temperature phonons in a three-dimensional superfluid Fermi gas whose acoustic dispersion is ωq = cq[1 + (γ/8)(ℏq/mc)^2 + higher-order terms], what replaces the Born-Markov perturbative damping rate when the curvature γ is of order T^2 or crosses zero, so that the cubic curvature term is comparable to higher-order dispersion and the self-energy is non-Markovian and non-Born? Determine Γq, or the appropriate non-exponential decay measure, in this small-curvature regime that is experimentally relevant near unitarity.

evidence.quote: we expect the system to have, in its ground state, a branch of acoustic excitation (by sound waves) that starts out linear in wavenumber q with a cubic correction, ωq = cq [1 + γ/8 (ħq/mc)2 + O(q4 ln q)]

The precise calculation of the damping rate Γq (or what takes its place for non-exponential decay, such as the inverse of the width of |〈 ˆbq(t)〉|2 at relative height 1/e) for these small values of curvature is, to our knowledge, an open question; it is of great experimental relevance, as the interaction strength leading to γ = 0 seems to be close to the unitary limit

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a three-dimensional homogeneous superfluid Fermi gas at low temperature T (with k_B = 1 absorbed) whose elementary excitations form an acoustic branch with dispersion

  ω_q = c q [ 1 + (γ/8)(ℏ q / m c)^2 + O(q^4 log q) ],

where c is the sound velocity, m the fermion mass, q the phonon wavenumber, and γ a dimensionless curvature parameter characterizing the cubic correction to the linear phonon dispersion. The phonon-phonon interaction is the standard cubic and quartic hydrodynamic coupling derived from the equation of state.

When γ is of order unity and positive (convex dispersion), the leading low-temperature damping rate Γ_q of a phonon mode of wavenumber q can be computed in the Born–Markov approximation (Beliaev–Landau processes), giving an exponential decay ⟨b̂_q(t)⟩ ∝ exp(−i ω_q t − Γ_q t /2) with Γ_q obtained from the imaginary part of the on-shell self-energy at lowest order in the interaction.

This Born–Markov treatment breaks down when |γ| becomes so small that the cubic curvature term (γ/8)(ℏq/mc)^2 is comparable to the next-order O(q^4 log q) dispersion terms, and when γ is of order T^2 (in natural units of (mc^2)^2), so that the self-energy is neither Markovian nor of Born form, and ⟨b̂_q(t)⟩ may exhibit non-exponential decay.

Problem. In this small-curvature regime (in particular near the interaction strength at which γ vanishes), determine the phonon damping rate Γ_q, or, when decay is non-exponential, an appropriate replacement such as the inverse of the half-width at relative height 1/e of |⟨b̂_q(t)⟩|^2 as a function of t, as a function of q, T, c, m, and the small parameter γ.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is stated by the authors of the survey on open questions for strongly interacting Fermi gases as an open question of experimental relevance near unitarity. A brief search did not identify a published derivation of the phonon damping rate in the small-curvature (γ ≈ 0 or γ ~ T^2) non-Markovian, non-Born regime for the 3D superfluid Fermi gas. Status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Open questions for strongly interacting Fermi gases with zero-range interactions
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems including the precise phonon damping rate for small acoustic curvature near unitarity.
status_evidence.claim: The authors explicitly identify the computation of Γ_q (or its non-exponential analog) in the small-curvature regime as an open question.
